vision.more.title: More
vision.more.intro: Slower models, trained only if you tick them and start a run, on the same folds as the others and scored on the same images. None becomes the default: each says what it gains over the linear probe, with an interval.
vision.more.conceptsHint: To make a concept from images: select them in the Gallery (or on the Map), then Save as concept.
vision.more.saveBody: A concept is something you can see in images, such as yellow edges or a cracked surface. The concept bottleneck (Model › Advanced › More) learns it; TCAV (Explain › More) tests whether the network uses it.
vision.more.saveTooFew: {count}: too few for now. The concept bottleneck needs 5 images or more, TCAV 20 or more; add images later by saving a larger selection under another name. The other images of the set are taken as without the concept.
vision.more.saveFew: {count} images: enough for the concept bottleneck (5 or more), not yet for TCAV (20 or more). The other images of the set are taken as without the concept.
vision.more.saveEnough: Enough for the concept bottleneck and for TCAV. The other images of the set are taken as without the concept.

vision.more.looksOwn: This is how the prototype network computed its score (ProtoPNet, Chen et al., 2019): each prototype is a patch of a real training image, not a post-hoc map.

vision.more.tcavTitle: TCAV: does a concept push the network towards a class?
vision.more.tcavIntro: A concept is a set of images (a group you saved, a true/false column, or a class). TCAV finds the direction of that concept inside the network, then counts how often moving along it raises each class's score, and tests that share against random directions (Kim et al., 2018).
vision.more.tcavRunning: Testing the concept against 10 random sets
vision.more.tcavFacts: {images} concept images against random sets of {random}; the concept's direction separates them {accuracy} of the time on held-out images; {layer}; {seconds} s.
vision.more.randomLegend: The bar is the share of the class's images whose score rises along the concept; the tick is the same share along random directions. Only a significant difference (p < 0.05) says the network uses the concept.
vision.more.trainingFacts: {epochs} epochs, the weights of epoch {best} kept (dotted line); {device}, {precision}; {seconds} s.
vision.more.conceptQuality: Concepts: how well they are read, how they push each class
vision.more.conceptQualityNote: Each concept is read from the image (AUC for a true/false concept, R² for a number), then the class reads the concepts only. A weak concept is one the images hardly show.
